niche: multi-employer agreement rate base for bargaining: the ordinary rate of pay rebuilt from rosters in contract cleaning, security and catering
answer: Open bargaining at 4.7 per cent on every Schedule A rate.
stakeholder_role: economist at a facilities services employers' federation

spine.entity: one rostered shift worked by an employee

world.org_type: employers' federation party to a multi-employer agreement

driver: The decisive quantity is what raising a floor obliges each unit to pay, which for units paid on a flat all-in arrangement is a shortfall tested per person per pay period against the floor-priced entitlement of the work actually done, so the cost curve is convex in the dial, and testing the flat amount against the floor, or netting the test over a year or a unit, finds no cost where the cost sits and sets the dial too high.
driver_concrete: The opening offer is the largest uniform increase in the Schedule A rates whose cost stays inside the council's mandate in cents per ordinary hour on the rate base; the cost is each member's shortfall below the raised rate on penalty-weighted hours, plus, for members paying one flat rate for every hour under the set-off clause, the amount by which each employee's fortnight falls short of the raised rates' entitlement for the shifts worked, so a flat rate several dollars above the raised minimum still costs money in the weekend and night fortnights.
stump: A competent solver recovers each member's rate from penalty-weighted hours, tests it against the raised Schedule A rate at each setting and finds the largest setting inside the mandate, reading the flat-rate members as clear because their rate sits above the raised minimum, so it never prices what each of their employees' fortnights would be entitled to and opens with an offer the mandate does not cover.

differentiation.task77: task77 v2 collapses a join that fans out to one row per person before netting coverage unit by unit; here nothing fans out, and the decisive move is a per-pay-period shortfall test of a flat all-in rate against a floor-priced entitlement, convex in the dial being set, which netting over the year or the employer erases.
differentiation.task93: The same decisive move, kept on purpose and hardened rather than redrawn: the first cut filed the flat-rate arrangement and its per-pay-period top-up as a clause, so the cost was a filed formula; this version files only a general pay-period rule, leaves the arrangement to arithmetic, and ships a closed costing that every method reproduces. If this version is solved the slot's world is retired, per the design note's stopping rule.
